cards.explanation: The people are astonished because His message had authority. Luke gives that reason: "They were astonished at His teaching, because His message had authority." Jesus wasn't just passing along thoughts. He spoke like His words carried weight. Picture me stamping a cookie and the dough actually obeying, friends. That would astonish me too.

The answer is True. The man cries out that he knows who Jesus is, and he calls Him "…the Holy One of God!" (Luke 4:34). He says it loud, right there in the synagogue. He asks, "Have You come to destroy us?" and then he names Jesus. Nobody had to introduce Jesus to that voice.

Jesus rebukes the demon. "Jesus rebuked the demon. 'Be silent!' He said. 'Come out of him!'" (Luke 4:35). Jesus doesn't argue and doesn't debate. He gives two short commands, and the demon comes out. The demon throws the man down before them all, but it comes out without harming him.

The answer is False. The demon throws the man down before them all, and it "…came out without harming him." (Luke 4:35). It looks scary, but the man isn't badly hurt. He's thrown down in front of everyone and still left unharmed, friends.

Jesus commands the unclean spirits. The people ask, "With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!" (Luke 4:36). They watched it happen with their own eyes. A demon had just obeyed Jesus in front of the whole synagogue.

Jesus is asked to help her. Luke says, "…they appealed to Jesus on her behalf…" (Luke 4:38). Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and somebody took it straight to Jesus. Good place to take it, friends.

The word is serve. "…she got up at once and began to serve them." (Luke 4:39). No slow recovery, no long nap. The fever left, and she was up. I can't even get out of bed after a cold without three days and a blanket.

The answer is False, friends. Jesus doesn't heal only a few. "…laying His hands on each one, He healed them." (Luke 4:40). At sunset, all who were ill with various diseases were brought to Him. Jesus doesn't stop at a few. He heals each one.

The word is Christ. Luke says Jesus "…would not allow them to speak, because they knew He was the Christ." (Luke 4:41). The demons were shouting, "You are the Son of God!" and Jesus rebuked them. They knew who He was, and He still didn't let them speak.

The word is leaving. The crowds "…came to Him and tried to keep Him from leaving." (Luke 4:42). Jesus had gone out to a solitary place at daybreak. The crowds were looking for Him, and they found Him there.

The reason Jesus gives is that it's why He was sent. He says, "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent." (Luke 4:43). He gives one reason, and it's about why He was sent. The crowds wanted Him to stay, and He kept to His purpose.
